Class RegionMath

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.RegionMath
@Internal public final class RegionMath extends Object
Pure coordinate resolver for M5 regions. Given explicit inputs — anchor-frame bounds (or screen dimensions), panel dimensions, and the current stacking prefix — returns the panel's screen-space origin, or Optional.empty() if the panel's extent exceeds the region's available space.

Pure by design. No registry state, no Panel references, no per-frame side effects. Enables /mkverify all to exercise the math with synthetic inputs without spinning up a screen or touching the RegionRegistry. See M5 design doc §9.1.

Public entry points map to a sentinel at the boundary. This class returns Optional<ScreenOrigin> for compositional clarity. The adapter pipeline (RegionRegistry) maps Optional.empty() to ScreenOrigin.OUT_OF_REGION so the region origin resolvers return a stable sentinel. See §6.5.

    • availableMenuHeight

      public static int availableMenuHeight(MenuRegion region, ScreenBounds b, int sh, int margin)
      OUTER available height (padding-inclusive) for a MenuContext region panel before it crosses the screen-edge margin, given the (chrome-extended) menu frame and the screen height. The height twin of availableMenuWidth(MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int) — mirrors resolveMenu(MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int, int, int, int)'s per-region Y geometry so a too-tall panel auto-scrolls into exactly the room its anchor leaves toward the screen edge, rather than rendering off-screen (then getting clamped over the frame). The caller subtracts the panel's 2×padding to get the content-height ceiling for Panel.setAvailableContentHeight(int).

      Like availableMenuWidth(MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int), the stacking prefix is ignored here — the budget is computed for the region's anchor edge (an over-estimate for the 2nd+ panel in a vertically-stacked adaptive set; single-panel and horizontal-flow regions are exact).

    • availableMenuWidth

      public static int availableMenuWidth(MenuRegion region, ScreenBounds b, int sw, int margin)
      OUTER available width (padding-inclusive) for a MenuContext region panel before it crosses the screen-edge margin, given the (chrome-extended) menu frame and the screen width. Mirrors resolveMenu(MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int, int, int, int)'s per-region anchor geometry so the budget and the origin agree on where the panel sits. The caller subtracts the panel's 2×padding to get the content budget for Panel.setAvailableContentWidth(int).

      Horizontal-flow regions (TOP/BOTTOM_ALIGN) ignore the stacking prefix here — the budget is computed for the region's anchor edge, an over-estimate for the 2nd+ panel in a horizontally-stacked adaptive set. That multi-panel-horizontal-adaptive case is rare; single-panel and all vertical-flow regions are exact.

    • availableScreenEdgeWidth

      public static int availableScreenEdgeWidth(int sw, int inset)
      OUTER available width for a screen-edge-anchored panel (HUD / VanillaScreen contexts). All such regions are inset RegionConstants.EDGE_INSET from one edge and should keep the same inset from the opposite edge, so the budget is the screen width minus the inset on both sides.

    • resolveScreenRegion

      public static ScreenOrigin resolveScreenRegion(ScreenRegion region, int sw, int sh, int pw, int ph, int margin)
      Places a pw × ph chrome panel at one of the nine ScreenRegion screen-edge spots, inset by margin from the edges it touches. Pure: the panel anchors to the SCREEN (not the content frame), so unlike resolveMenu(MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int, int, int, int) it always resolves — a screen-edge spot is on-screen by construction (a panel wider/taller than the screen minus margins simply overhangs the far edge, the degenerate case).

      The X axis: LEFT spots pin to margin; CENTER spots centre on the screen width; RIGHT spots pin to the right margin. The Y axis mirrors it (TOP / middle / BOTTOM). Used by both the standalone-screen (MKScreen) and custom-container (MainRegionLayout) chrome paths, so a Back button / title anchors to the screen identically in both.

    • resolveMenu

      public static Optional<ScreenOrigin> resolveMenu(MenuRegion region, ScreenBounds bounds, int pw, int ph, int prefix, int sw, int sh)
      Resolves a MenuContext region panel's origin. Returns Optional.empty() when prefix + panel_extent exceeds the region's available space (menu height for side regions, menu width for top/bottom regions).
      Parameters:
      region - the MenuContext region the panel belongs to
      bounds - the vanilla menu's container-frame bounds this frame
      pw - the panel's width (from Panel.getWidth())
      ph - the panel's height (from Panel.getHeight())
      prefix - total axial extent of visible preceding panels in the same region, plus one RegionConstants.MENU_STACK_GAP per preceding panel
      sw - GUI-scaled screen width (Pass 3 — for the screen safe-area overflow gate; edge regions extend toward the screen edge, not the menu edge)
      sh - GUI-scaled screen height

    • resolveHud

      public static Optional<ScreenOrigin> resolveHud(HudRegion region, int sw, int sh, int pw, int ph, int prefix)
      Resolves a HUD-region panel's origin. All HUD regions flow vertically; overflow is measured against the region's axial capacity (screen height minus edge insets, halved for center-anchored regions).
      Parameters:
      region - the HUD region
      sw - GUI-scaled screen width
      sh - GUI-scaled screen height
      pw - the panel's width
      ph - the panel's height
      prefix - total height of visible preceding panels in the same region, plus one RegionConstants.MENU_STACK_GAP per preceding panel

    • resolveVanillaScreen

      public static Optional<ScreenOrigin> resolveVanillaScreen(ScreenRegion region, int sw, int sh, int pw, int ph, int prefix)
      Region-relative placement for ScreenRegions on a vanilla non-container screen (Options, Controls, KeyBinds, etc.).

      Parallel to resolveHud(HudRegion, int, int, int, int, int): anchored to the screen's GUI-scaled w × h, with RegionConstants.EDGE_INSET from each edge. The only semantic difference vs HUD positioning is that vanilla screens have NO crosshair behind them — the ScreenRegion.CENTER region anchors to the true screen center, no crosshair clearance offset.

      Returns Optional.empty() when prefix + ph exceeds the available axis extent — caller treats as "this panel doesn't fit in its region this frame" and skips render. ScreenOrigin.OUT_OF_REGION is the adapter-side sentinel for the same condition.

      Parameters:
      region - the destination region
      sw - GUI-scaled screen width
      sh - GUI-scaled screen height
      pw - the panel's width (padding-inclusive)
      ph - the panel's height (padding-inclusive)
      prefix - total height of visible preceding panels in the same region, plus one RegionConstants.MENU_STACK_GAP per preceding panel
